Hello there! If you're here, you may be wondering what the heck a fingerboard is, of all things. A fingerboard is like a skateboard, but.. for your fingers! Most of us probably remember Tech Decks, which is where a lot of us got our start in fingerboarding.

For some of us, it didn't stop there. People wanted better than the plastic mold tech decks, and so they started making their own. Forgive me for not knowing the history very well as I was still a lot younger then, but basically, people started making their own decks, and eventually trucks, wheels, bushings, etc.

Today, there are well known companies like:

  • Flatface

  • Blackriver

  • Yellowood

And there are many other smaller companies run by people with a passion, generally based on Instagram. Companies like: Homewood, Redwolf, Levelup, Zink (now Besour), Woob, Beastpants, and so many more.

Myself, I make decks once in a while, but haven't as of late since I don't have a workspace. My instagram is @heartwoodfb. The community on instagram is pretty big for such a small hobby, and if you wanna see really good fingerboarding and some rad stuff like that, follow people on instagram and just get involved.

Most of the fingerboard forums out there on the web are pretty dead. I came into the scene late, and the only two I ever knew of were FFI and FBHQ

A good place to go for FB news is Unite Fingerboarding.

There's also a subreddit for fingerboarding, but it's very dead, and I really think that with the community on voat, if any of you out there are fingerboarders or think you might enjoy the hobby, then please feel free to come here and create some discussion and grow the culture.

As a last note, if you might want to get into fingerboarding, and think that the price of blackriver, flatface, and other products may deter you, check out Broken Knuckle they have some china completes or individual parts for your setup at much cheaper prices, which would be great for a beginner.

I'll try to edit this in the future with any relevant content I can think of and any suggestions from the community.
